# Team platform instructions

## response.style

Keep answers direct. State the recommended option first, then the reasoning
behind it. Avoid hedging language when the evidence already supports one
conclusion, and say plainly when it does not.

## review.approval

A change to a shared interface needs one platform reviewer's approval before
it merges, recorded against the exact revision reviewed. A reviewer checks
the change against the interface's own contract, not against personal taste.

## escalation

When a decision affects more than one repository, raise it in the platform
channel before committing, and record the outcome against the concern it
resolved so a later reader can find why the choice was made.

## formatting

Prefer short paragraphs over long ones, and prefer a worked example over an
abstract description when both are available. Code samples should compile
against the platform's current pinned toolchain version, not an older one.

## journal mode

The platform's shared volume does not honour fullfsync, so a rollback
journal is the safe default there; write-ahead logging is fine on a volume
that does honour it, and each repository states which volume it runs on.

## incident handling

Open an incident record the moment a shared service degrades, even before
the cause is known. Close it only after the fix is verified in the same
environment the incident was observed in, and link the record it resolved.

## onboarding

A new team member reads this file and the repository's own instructions
before their first change, and asks in the platform channel when the two
disagree, rather than guessing which one applies. A short pairing session
in the first week answers most questions, and the buddy stays reachable
for that month, available for anything left unclear.

members.text:
# Repository instructions

## response.style

State the recommended option first, then the evidence behind it. Keep the
first paragraph free of hedging when the evidence already supports one
conclusion, and name the open question plainly when it does not.

## review.approval

A change to a public interface needs one maintainer's approval before it
merges, recorded against the exact revision reviewed. A reviewer checks the
change against this file's own rules, not against a personal preference.

## testing

Run the test suite before every commit and report its output, not only
whether it passed. A change with no test coverage states why none applies.

## journal mode

This repository's local state database uses a rollback journal by default;
write-ahead logging is the alternative when a volume supports fullfsync,
and the choice is recorded against the concern it resolves.

## escalation

When a decision affects more than this repository, raise it in the shared
platform channel before committing, and link the outcome to the concern it
resolved so a later reader can find why the choice was made.
